quote: Lemma 4.3. Assume Y1 ~ GLSE1(µ1, σ1, δ1, ψ, α, β, H), Y2 ~ GLSE1(µ2, σ2, δ2, ψ, α, β, H). (1) If µ2 − µ1 + β(z)(δ2 − δ1) ≥ 0 for all z and σ1 = σ2, then Y1 ≤st Y2. (2) If Y1 ≤st Y2 and density generator g1 satisfies Assumption 4.1, then µ1 + E(β(Z))δ1 ≤ µ2 + E(β(Z))δ2 and σ1 = σ2.
family: Univariate generalized location-scale mixture of elliptical (GLSE) distributions, common ψ, α, β, H
compared: Y1 vs Y2 (univariate)

hypotheses.text: Assumption 4.1 on g1 (tail control of density generator)

conclusion.direction: Y1 ≤_st Y2; conversely st order implies the mean-type inequality and σ1 = σ2

quote: Example 4.4. We consider the special case of univariate GLSE distribution to illustrate the results in Lemma 4.3. The survival functions of the GHSS distributions under three parameter setting are plotted in Figure 1(a). It is easy to check that the conditions in Lemma 4.3(1) are satisfied, and thus agrees with the usual stochastic ordering among these three distributions displayed in the plot. Moreover, Figure 1(b) provides a counterexample showing that the survival functions of these distributions cross with each other if the scale parameters of the three distributions are not identical.

hypotheses.text: Lemma 4.3(1) conditions hold in Figure 1(a); violated σ-equality in Figure 1(b)

conclusion.direction: st ordering verified in (a); survival curves cross in (b) when σ's differ

quote: Theorem 4.6. Let Y1, Y2 follow (18). We have the following conclusions: (1) If µ1 = µ2, δ1 = δ2 and Σ2 − Σ1 is positive semi-definite, then Y1 ≤cx (≤lcx, ≤ilcx) Y2. quote: Example 4.8. Figure 2(b) provides a counterexample under the setting (µ1, σ1, δ1) = (0, 1, 0.5) and (µ2, σ2, δ2) = (1, 2, −0.5). quote: Theorem 4.11. Let Y1, Y2 follow (18). The following statements hold: (1) If µ1 = µ2, δ1 = δ2, σ1,ii ≤ σ2,ii for 1 ≤ i ≤ n and σ1,ij = σ2,ij for 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n, then Y1 ≤ccx Y2.
